data.translation: Uncle Isho: Sir, there were makers of arak. They used to bring the raisins and put them in those things, in the kettles, or rather in those things, in big barrels, and do things to them... They would work them into a mash, and afterwards put them in the kettles and boil them, and distil illicit arak. Then a time came when the government prohibited it. They had prohibited arak; the Unhisar [State Monopoly] had appeared. Special arak used to come from Diyarbakir. Whoever was caught with illicit arak in his possession, they would punish him.

summary: Across Ritter, JTM, MAC and Lahdo, explicit repairs (hne ... markawle; kohno ... korəḥmolan; məhnənwa mačəlṣiwa) support a productive placeholder verb. Specific edition renderings such as quälen, schlaff werden, beschälen and rescue do not by themselves establish lexical senses.

Detransitive forms occur with affected subjects, deliberate agents, l-suffixes and ʕal-/b-complements. They are not uniformly patient-subject constructions. The inherited Detransitive examples have no sense numbers; proposed Detransitive 1 explicitly labels their common placeholder function without moving or renumbering any inherited example.
Infectum-wa includes habitual task sequences and counterfactuals. A new Detransitive Infectum-wa box is supported by both MAC Hanna Dewo/143 and Ritter 99/53.

Repeated hny ruḥe has differing contextual actions (self-praise, intervention, chess gestures), so no fixed idiom is added. Nominal hno with sym is distinct from the finite placeholder. No new light-verb collocation is asserted.
The m-prefixed forms məhnalle, məhnole, Mahnalle and gmahnile cannot safely be assigned to II merely from the prefix; II's established congratulatory meaning is independently supported at 56/65.
Round 1 already established Detransitive Infectum-wa and numbered its placeholder sense 1. Jan's missing-form claims for that series are obsolete; only II Infectum is new after round 1.
The placeholder followed by saymiwonne taḥriš or layfənwanne leaves the intended action recoverable from discourse. It does not lexicalize fermentation, manipulation, repair or a funeral rite.
Kəmhanenalle d xaliṣi has an explicit congratulatory reason and is reinforced by bəšra kəmbašrinalle. This supports II.1 independently of uncertain m-prefixed placeholders.
The inherited unnumbered I Detransitive examples are counted under round-1 placeholder label 1, following that proposal's explicit mapping. No inherited text or sense numbering is changed.
Confirm the paradigm and stem of məhnalle (JTM 1.1/21), məhnole (MAC Hanna Dewo/87), Mahnalle (MAC NE Keze/25), Məhnalle (76/41), and gmahnile (74/58).
Is success/efficacy məhne in JTM 5.1/8 and 115/179 a continuation of etymological hny 'profit/avail', or a lexicalized use of the placeholder? Confirm the extent of b-iḏ- government.
Are məhno at 78/97 and hne at 115/148, 115/301 finite forms or nominal/discourse placeholders? Confirm hnewalle, hnən, hnutu and hnalle at 115/108 before adding them as form evidence.
Please segment koməhnənne (73/429), məhnene (78/51), and məhnənne (82/9); establish the role of affected suffixes, especially in agentive Detransitive forms.
Is kəmhanenolox at Jan 1.35/1438 an ordinary congratulatory reaction to the correct title, a dialectal placeholder, or a form of the I Detransitive series? Context does not justify a new II sense.
Confirm the segmentation and affected suffixes of Məhnewonne, məhnewonne, məhnewole and məhnənwanne, retaining round-1 Detransitive filing provisionally rather than deriving patient-subject meaning.
At Jan 3.18/401 Məhnewayle has unclear person and segmentation; is it an inflected placeholder or a disfluent nominal mə hno sequence? It is not used to establish a box.
Provide verified Jan translations; machine-English contextual expansions are withheld from the examples.
Restore the adjective ending in sinnloser Verbstamm
rationale: The attributive adjective before masculine singular Verbstamm requires -er without an article. This corrects the grammatical slip while retaining the inherited term.

summary: Placeholder forms cover favorable and adverse states, agentive processing, bodily effects, hospitality, and euphemistic horse breeding. These are contextual participant/event extensions, not separate lexical meanings.

Jan's funeral, distilling, building and candle-making contexts reinforce the round-1 Detransitive placeholder proposal. Their object suffixes and deliberate human actors corroborate the earlier agentive forms without giving the omitted operations lexical senses.
Congratulation extends to deceased recipients who have escaped suffering; this changes the recipient and context, not the lexical act. The explicit good-news paraphrase confirms the reading.
